basis: Operator decision 2026-10-21 ('ship it'): publish with an honest unresolved-licence label rather than wait for a WHO answer. The licence position changed on re-examination. WHO's general publishing policy names CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO for WHO publications, but FluNet is a dataset, and the FluNet tool page links a 'Data policy' whose terms for WHO data compilations, aggregations, evaluations and analyses (a) restrict use and distribution to public health purposes, (b) state that any alteration or modification of the Datasets 'may be made only with the prior written authorization of WHO', and (c) state that the Datasets may not be transferred to a third party except within the Licensed Use. This release is a substantial alteration - a re-grained country-week panel, a derived binary label, a temporal partition. No dataset-specific licence was found on the FluNet page, in the xMART metadata CSV, or in the API response headers. CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO cannot be applied by a non-intergovernmental publisher in any case, so asserting it over our compilation was a claim we could not support. The operator accepted the residual risk explicitly: the artifact is published with no licence asserted over the source rows, a plain statement of the ambiguity, and a documented takedown route.

compilation.scope: Our contribution - the row selection, the derived binary label, the temporal partition, the gating rules and the packaging - is our work, but it is not dedicated under any licence here. We lack the standing to apply CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (that licence may only be applied by an intergovernmental organisation) and we hold no written authorisation from WHO for the alteration. Nothing in this release grants you rights over the source rows, and nothing here may be presented as CC0, public domain, an open licence, or an official WHO product.

source.status: No dataset-specific licence established. WHO's general publishing policy names CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO for WHO publications; WHO's terms for data compilations (linked from the FluNet page as 'Data policy') require prior written authorisation for alterations and restrict transfer to third parties. FluNet states no dataset-specific licence, and its dataset carries no licence field in the metadata CSV or the API response. Redistribution of this derived compilation therefore rests on the operator's recorded risk acceptance, not on a grant from the publisher.
evidence: [https://www.who.int/tools/flunet, read 2026-10-21] the tool page links 'Data policy' and states no dataset-specific licence; the full-dataset CSV download is the publisher's own link.

[https://www.who.int/about/policies/publishing/data-policy/terms-and-conditions, read 2026-10-21] clause 04: 'Any other alteration or modification of the Datasets (including abbreviations, additions, or deletions) may be made only with the prior written authorization of WHO.' clause 05: 'You will not sell or otherwise transfer the Datasets and/or data contained therein to any third party, except within the Licensed Use.' clause 01 grants use and distribution 'for public health purposes'.

[https://www.who.int/about/policies/publishing/copyright, read 2026-10-21] general publishing policy: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO for WHO publications, and the note that this licence 'can only be used by organizations established by a treaty or other instrument governed by international law' - i.e. not by this project.
[WHO xMART metadata CSV for FluNet and the VIW_FNT response headers, read 2026-10-21] no licence, terms or copyright field is present.

operator_acceptance.note: The operator was shown the specific WHO clauses, the absence of a dataset-specific licence, and the fact that CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO cannot be applied by this project, and chose to publish with an honest unresolved-licence label and a takedown route rather than wait for a WHO reply. This is a risk acceptance; no publisher grant is claimed anywhere in the release.
